      "key": "two_sided_path_and_erasure_evidence",
      "statement": "Every required authoritative composition needs an exact ordinary-path witness in the deployed, installed or otherwise runnable Product; every material superseded, duplicate, fallback, bypass or other forbidden production path must be absent, unreachable or refused at its declared boundary. Successor success does not prove predecessor removal. Production closure covers exact form/configuration and transitive imports, exports, package paths, switches, registries, fallbacks, consumers, generated runtime artifacts, recovery and fresh-process reconstruction; no obsolete, bypass, fallback or rival production path may remain reachable in the claimed scope. Assurance/source closure covers relied-on source consumers, fixtures, proof scripts, generators, mutations and tooling; obsolete consumers must neither falsely establish closure nor reintroduce removed paths. Such capability remains an assurance defect even outside production. Proportionate safe path-sensitive assurance checks that disabling the authoritative path prevents scenario success, forcing/restoring a rival yields refusal or a detected counterexample, material interface/owner-result corruption is detected at its owner, and obsolete-path removal preserves the outcome subject to the deletion exception. Forbidden-path success falsifies the path claim. A negative-path mutation without isolation, restoration and subject revalidation invalidates its own assurance basis.",
